clauses.label: (a )
clauses.text:
(a ) C ivilia n  manpower m obilization.  Develop plans and issue 
guidance designed to utilize to the maximum extent civilian manpower 
resources, such plans and guidance to be developed with the active 
participation and assistance o f the States and local political sub­
divisions thereof, and of other organizations and agencies concerned 
with the mobilization o f the people o f the United States. Such plans 
shall include, but not necessarily be limited to :
(.1). Manpower management.  Recruitment, selection and referral, 
training, employment stabilization (including appeals procedures), 
proper utilization, and determination o f the skill categories critical 
to meeting the labor requirements o f defense and essential civilian 
activities.

(2) P rio ritie s. Procedures for translating survival and production 
urgencies into manpower priorities to be used as guides for allocating 
available workers.

(3) N ational guidance. Technical guidance to States for the utili­
zation o f the nationwide system o f public employment offices and 
other appropriate agencies for screening, recruiting, and referring

=== PDF page 17 of 80 ===
FEDERAL REGISTERTuesday, F e b ru a ry  20, 1962
workers, and for other appropriate activities to meet mobilization and 
civil defense needs in each community.

(4) Im p rovin g m obilization base.  Programs for more effective 
utilization o f limited manpower resources, and in cooperation with 
other appropriate agencies, programs for recruitment, training, allo­
cation, and utilization of persons possessing specialized competence 
or aptitude in acquiring such competence.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text:
(b) Wage and salary stabilization.  Develop plans and procedures 
for wage and salary stabilization and for the national and field organi­
zation necessary for the administration of such a program in an emer­
gency, including investigation, compliance and appeals procedures; 
statistical studies of wages, salaries and prices for policy decisions and 
to assist operating stabilization agencies to carry out their functions.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text:
(c) W orker incentives and protection.  Develop plans and proce­
dures for wage and salary compensation and death and disability com­
pensation for authorized civil defense workers and, as appropriate, 
measures for unemployment payments, re-employment rights, and oc­
cupational safety, and other protection and incentives for the civilian 
labor force during an emergency.

clauses.label: (d )
clauses.text:
(d ) Resources. Periodically assess manpower resources in total, 
by specific skills categories and occupations, and by geographical 
locations, in order to estimate availability under an emergency situa­
tion, analyze resource estimates in relation to estimated requirements 
in order to identify problem areas, and develop appropriate recom­
mendations and programs. Provide data and assistance before and 
after attack for national resource evalutio'n purposes of the Office of 
Emergency Planning.

clauses.label: (e)
clauses.text:
(e) Requirements. Develop, in coordination with manpower-using 
■agencies* plans, procedures and standards for presenting claims for 
civilian manpower; periodically obtain and analyze or make esti­
mates o f requirements for manpower, in total and by specific skill 
categories and occupations currently and for any emergency, taking 
into account the estimates of needs for military and civilian purposes; 
and advise other agencies on the manpower implications o f alternative 
program decisions. Such evaluation shall take into consideration the ' 
geographical distribution of requirements under emergency conditions.

clauses.label: ( f )
clauses.text:
( f )  Glaimancy. Prepare plans to claim materials, equipment, sup­
plies and services needed in support o f assigned responsibilities and 
other essential functions of the Department from appropriate agen­
cies, and work with such agencies in developing programs to insure 
the availability of such resources in an emergency.

clauses.label: (g )
clauses.text:
(g ) S k ill development and training.  Initiate current action pro­
grams to overcome .or offset present or anticipated manpower deficien­
cies including those identified as a result of resources and requirements 
studies.

clauses.label: (h )
clauses.text:
(h ) Labor-management relations.  Develop, after consultation with 
the Department of Commerce, the Department o f Defense, the Na­
tional Labor Relations Board, the Federal Mediation and Concilia­
tion Service, the National Mediation Board, and other appropriate 
agencies and groups including representatives o f labor and manage­
ment, plans and procedures including organization plans for the main­
tenance o f effective labor-management relations during a national 
emergency.

clauses.label: (i)
clauses.text:
(i) Damage assessment. Maintain a capability to assess the effects 
of attack upon manpower resources, departmental installations, and 
State Employment Security agencies, both at national and field levels, 
and provide data to the Department of Defense.

clauses.label: (j )
clauses.text:
(j )  C ritica l occupations. Develop and maintain a list of critical 
occupations for use, when appropriate, with lists of essential activi­
ties as developed by the Department o f Commerce. W ith the Secre­
tary o f Defense, the Director of Selective Service System, and such 
other persons as the President may designate, the Secretary shall 
develop policies applicable to the deferment of registrants whose em­
ployment in occupations or activities is necessary to the maintenance 
of the national health, safety, or interest.No. 3 5-----3

=== PDF page 18 of 80 ===
1534 THE PRESIDENT

clauses.label: Sec. 3.
clauses.text:
Sec. 3. Research. W ithin the framework of Federal research ob­
jectives, supervise or conduct research directly concerned with carry­
ing out emergency preparedness responsibilities, designate represent­
atives fo r necessary ad hoc or task force groups, ana provide advice 
and assistance to other agencies in planning for research in areas 
involving the Department’s interest.

clauses.label: Sec. 4.
clauses.text:
Sec. 4. Functional Guidance.  The Secretary, in carrying out the  
functions assigned in this order, shall be guided by the following:

clauses.label: (a )
clauses.text:
(a ) Interagency cooperation.  The Secretary shall assume the 
initiative in developing over-all civilian manpower mobilization pro­
grams and in coordinating the programs o f other departments and 
agencies which have responsibility for any segment o f such activities. 
H e shall utilize to the maximum those capabilities o f other agencies 
qualified to perform of assist in the performance of assigned functions 
by contractual or other agreements. Such programs snail be in con­
sonance with national civil defense plans, programs and operations of 
the Department of Defense under Executive Order No. 10952*

clauses.label: (b )
clauses.text:
(b ) Presidential coordination.  The Director of the Office o f Emer­
gency Planning shall advise and assist the President in determining 
policy for, and assist him in coordinating the performance o f functions 
under this order with the total national prepardness program.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text:
(c) Em ergency planning.  Emergency plans and programs, and 
emergency organization structure required thereby, shall be developed 
as an integral part of the continuing activities of the Department of 
Labor on the basis that it w ill have the responsibility for carrying 
out such programs during an emergency. The Secretary shall be 
prepared to implement all appropriate plans developed under this 
order. Modifications and temporary organizational changes, based 
on emergency conditions, w ill be in accordance with policy determina­
tion by the President.

clauses.label: Sec. 5.
clauses.text:
Sec. 5. Emergency Actions.  Nothing in this order shall be con­
strued as conferring authority under Title I I I  of the Federal Civil 
Defense A ct o f 1950, as amended, or otherwise, to put into effect any 
emergency plan, procedure, policy, program or course o f action pre­
pared or developed pursuant to this order. Such authority is 
reserved to the President.

clauses.label: Sec. 6.
clauses.text:
Sec. 6. Redelegation.  The Secretary is hereby authorized to re­
delegate within the Department of Labor the functions hereinabove 
assigned to him.
Sec. T. P r io r  Actions. To the extent of any inconsistency between 
the provisions o f any prior order and the provisions of this order, the 
latter shall control. Emergency Preparedness Order No. 8 (heretofore 
issued by the Director, Office of Civil and Defense Mobilization) (26 
F.R. 660-661), is hereby revoked.

versions.research_rationale: EO 11000 (signed 1962-02-16, 27 FR 1532-1534), read in full from the held official FR text: Sec. 1 Scope: civilian manpower mobilization, wage and salary stabilization, worker incentives, manpower resources and requirements, training, labor-management relations, critical occupations; Sec. 2 Functions (a)-(j); Sec. 3 Research; Sec. 4 Functional Guidance (a)-(c); Sec. 5 Emergency Actions (no authority to put plans into effect); Sec. 6 Redelegation; Sec. 7 Prior Actions (printed 'Sec. T.' in the text layer; this order controls over inconsistent prior orders; Emergency Preparedness Order No. 8 revoked). It has no term or sunset. EO 11490 sec. 3015 item (8) revokes it, effective on signing 1969-10-28 (official text, PDF page 95). Inventory: the dossier's clauses omit the Sec. 1 Scope and some section lead-ins and run some sections together; one override restates the inventory as 7 section clauses with no gap or overlap from Sec. 1 to the end of the Prior Actions section. D6 / earlier-end and later-amendment test: the OFR catalog records a 'See' note to EO 10952 (the 1961 civil-defense order the text cites) and the EO 11490 revocation; the OLRC note at 42 U.S.C. 5195 records only the EO 11490 revocation; the by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR order texts finds one order naming EO 11000, EO 11091 sec. 4(a) (Civil Service Commission plans 'shall be in consonance with national manpower policies and plans developed pursuant to Executive Order No. 11000'), which relies on the order and amends nothing; the other hits are its own heading printed at the end of EO 10999's held page text, dollar and pay-table figures (EO 8431-8433, 9456, 10145, 10174, 10286, 10287, 11119, 11413, 12387) and index page numbers in EO 9602; the full EO 11490 text names it only in sec. 3015. EO 11051 (1962-09-27) sec. 601 does not list it, and none of EO 11087-11095 (February 26, 1963) or EO 11310 (1966) names it. No order amended, suspended or ended any clause between 1962-02-16 and 1969-10-28, so no later event is attached. The Prior Actions section's revocation of an OCDM Emergency Preparedness Order was executed on issuance; revoking this order does not revive it. Savings: transferred_or_accrued (see savings_residuals).

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record LSP-EO_11490 (EO 11490, 34 FR 17567-17599, official FR text of FR-1969-10-30.pdf PDF pages 63-95 held by jobs/source-ladder, read in full; the American Presidency Project transcription was not used): sec. 101 says the order 'consolidates the assignment of emergency preparedness functions to various departments and agencies heretofore contained in the 21 Executive orders and 2 Defense Mobilization orders listed in Section 3015' and that 'Assignments have been adjusted to conform to changes in organization'; sec. 102(b) charges every department and agency with continuity-of-government planning; Parts 2-29 re-assign agency functions (Part 6 Post Office, Part 7 Interior, Part 8 Agriculture, Part 10 Labor, Part 11 Health, Education, and Welfare, Part 13 Transportation including civil aviation, Part 18 FCC including electromagnetic-radiation control of non-Government stations); Part 30 sets general provisions. Sec. 3014 ('Retention of Existing Authority') preserves existing assignments of functions 'Except as provided in Section 3015', so it expressly does not reach the revoked orders; sec. 3015 revokes 21 Executive orders and 2 Defense Mobilization orders without exception. There is no effective-date, pending-matter, transition or savings clause for any revoked order. Own-residual check, reading EO 11000 in full: it assigned to the Secretary of Labor national emergency preparedness planning functions (scope, functions, cooperation with the Department of Defense under EO 10952, research, functional guidance), disclaimed any authority to put plans into effect (Emergency Actions), allowed redelegation, and in its Prior Actions section revoked OCDM Emergency Preparedness Order No. 8 (26 F.R. 660-661). EO 11490 Part 10 (Department of Labor) re-assigns the same department's or agency's emergency preparedness functions, adjusted to later changes in organization (sec. 101); that is a new assignment by the consolidating order, not a continuation of EO 11000. Plans and programs developed before 1969-10-28 are completed acts. The revocation of Emergency Preparedness Order No. 8 (26 F.R. 660-661) was executed in 1962 and is not undone by revoking EO 11000. State transferred_or_accrued records the carry-forward of the assignment into EO 11490; no clause of EO 11000 continues. SECTION 501. Functions.

The Attorney General shall perform the following emergency preparedness functions:

  (1) Emergency documents and measures. Provide advice, as appropriate, with respect to any emergency directive or procedure prepared by a department or agency as a part of its emergency preparedness function.

  (2) Industry support.
